title: The Impressionist Art Movement
text: Impressionism was a 19th-century art movement characterized by relatively small, thin yet visible brush strokes, open composition, emphasis on accurate depiction of light, and ordinary subject matter. The movement originated in France with artists including Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Camille Pissarro, Edgar Degas, and Berthe Morisot. The term 'Impressionism' derives from Monet's painting Impression, Sunrise (1872), which critics initially used mockingly. Impressionists typically painted outdoors (en plein air) to capture natural light. The movement broke with the academic tradition of smooth, polished surfaces and historical or mythological subjects, paving the way for modern art movements.
